I will do it much like last year, just trim and add a little where I think it pays. On my 7.5 mu, I cannot gamble. If the crop goes weak because I saved one bag of fertilizer, that loss is bigger than wasting a bit of fertilizer. I have farmed here 40 years, and I mostly look at what the men around me do when their field comes out good. With well water in hand, I am not as scared of dry spells, so I will keep the land fed and water on time. For cotton, I will put the better land and more care there because cotton needs watching all season. Wheat and maize, I will do the usual way that works around here, with enough base fertilizer and one or two topdressings. I will not play with old seed if the hybrid or improved seed did well in nearby fields. My place is only 7.5 mu and just two people at home, so I will keep the plan steady, not fancy: plough or rotary where it saves labor, enough fertilizer to keep the crop standing strong, and sprays when insects or disease show up, not waiting too long.
